approach.method_basis: The Parent keeps a forest of molecular graph-edit paths rooted in the supplied observations. Each occurrence stores real completed returns and separate pending reservations. New terminal molecules are bought directly, and their normalized scores update every occurrence on their actual paths. Existing branches are selected using count-fingerprint similarity to share sibling mean returns and completed/pending evidence density. Its widening rule currently treats completed and still-pending visits alike when deciding whether another child may be generated.
approach.novelty: Make branch growth depend only on completed feedback. Pending reservations will continue to discourage redundant selections, but will no longer unlock new siblings before their scores arrive. This changes the information used to grant an action, while keeping the widening constants and sibling mean selector. There are no finalized same-Parent siblings in the brief; the parallel best-return ticket instead changes the exploitation statistic and retains pending-aware widening. The prediction is that delaying unsupported branching increases actual repeated feedback on retained prefixes, which may improve later search progress.

hypothesis: Completed-feedback progressive widening on the inherited sibling-kernel tree: for an ordinary graph occurrence v, authorize another normal child iff child_count(v) < max(1,floor(1.5*(N_v+1)^0.5)), with N_v counting only actual completed returns, including the supplied root receipt at initial roots. Replace the Parent N_v+O_v input only at this consumer. Pending O and sibling pending density P retain their inherited exploration and reservation roles; they never become rewards. Thus a newly started, unobserved terminal cannot itself grant a new sibling. Narrower branching should concentrate later real returns on existing occurrences; whether this improves useful search remains a separate prediction.

finding_summary.headline: Completed-only widening increases repeat feedback but fails the registered useful-conversion test
finding_summary.insights:
Removing permission from pending work really does redirect visits, but the additional repetition is largely within a batch: repeated nonroot updates with earlier-batch support fell from 5,408 to 4,979, while updates sharing an earlier receipt from the same batch rose from 876 to 2,383. These categories overlap when a prefix has both kinds of history. Terminals supported by any earlier-batch return fell from 3,090 to 3,037. Thus a larger final repeated-occurrence fraction does not establish more rounds of adaptive learning. The tree also went deeper: maximum generated depth rose from seven to the fixed cap of twelve, with fourteen failed normal routes but no stored or emergency fallback. Most nonroot occurrences still had only one return (9,753 of 13,024), and retaining the inherited fresh rollouts kept total nonroot creation almost unchanged.

The molecular evidence shows broad scaffold coverage, not scaffold collapse: generic scaffold coverage stayed at 1,832 and typed coverage changed from 2,481 to 2,451. Both size tails increased, from 469 to 502 tiny proposals and from 450 to 475 proposals above fifty heavy atoms. Together with the unchanged initial optimum in all median_2 sessions and the lost higher docking observations, this points to a limitation in preserving useful connected arrangements while proposing new edits. Proposal operators or a search scheme that preserve and refine promising molecular arrangements could address that limitation; simply concentrating additional returns on prefixes did not do so here. The literature-derived completed/pending distinction and visit-dependent action growth operated, but their published domains supply no molecular performance guarantee. This result settles the registered conversion prediction for this particular widening law and controller composition. It leaves open whether a different proposal or selection mechanism can use persistent trajectory feedback effectively; it does not undo the Parent’s established sibling-sharing activation or decide the future of the wider approach.
finding_summary.results: All fifteen Search sessions completed. The new law suppressed 1,993 pending-only expansion permissions across 11,194 ordinary decisions, including 1,316 at occurrences with no completed return. Every audited width, route-credit ledger and sibling-selector calculation matched its registered rule. The final fraction of nonroot occurrences with at least two real returns increased from 2,440/13,049 (18.70%) to 3,175/13,024 (24.38%), and repeated-prefix terminal feedback rose slightly from 3,298/4,350 to 3,316/4,350. These activation and repetition predictions hold. Useful conversion fails: incumbent gain per optimizer evaluation fell from 0.0003555903 to 0.0003047999, and late-half gain fell from 0.735300 over twelve improvements to 0.428153 over seven. Mean final Top1 fell from 0.3116133 to 0.2968841, a paired change of −0.0147292 against the registered +0.002 target. Seed-macro changes were +0.0530795, +0.0066911 and −0.1039583. Three task means rose, median_2 stayed at its initial best, and docking fell in every seed, with mean loss 0.230566. The Child remains 0.310146 below the separate formal Anchor mean of 0.6070303. Frozen task-safety margins were not supplied, so a formal safety verdict is unavailable; every signed task/seed difference and its dispersion is retained.

molecular.headline: Broad ring and aromatic chemistry with persistent size extremes, reactive linkages and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of n-ea747c09699e against code Parent n-4e4e248bd6bd on the frozen Search panel: seeds 0, 1 and 2, five tasks, 300 observations per session including ten supplied initial records, batch ten. context.comparison marks Child evaluation complete and Parent pairing complete. All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectories and their molecular diagnostic logs were read; no paths, task cells or Parent comparisons are missing. Population descriptors exclude initial molecules: 4,350 actual optimizer proposals on each side. No unpurchased candidates or passive alternatives are treated as evaluated molecules. The output includes diaryl pyrazoline/thioamide families, indole carboxamides, fused aza-aromatics, dicarbonyl nitrogen heterocycles, sulfonylated saturated nitrogen rings, polyaryl esters and oxygen-rich acetal assemblies. Ring chemistry is abundant: 3,575 Child proposals contain rings versus 3,598 Parent; aromatic atoms occur in 2,734 versus 2,788. The digest's ring-closure rates span 0.7736 to 0.8552 and aromatic-text rates 0.5563 to 0.7138, consistent with broad cyclic coverage. Child heavy atoms span 1 to 119 with median 25, versus Parent 1 to 116 with median 25. Below-six-heavy-atom proposals increase from 469 to 502 and above-fifty proposals from 450 to 475: both tails persist even though the central size is unchanged. Nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold identities are 2,451/1,832 versus 2,481/1,832, so there is broad structural coverage rather than a collapsed ring vocabulary. Existing fragment-excluded within-batch count-Tanimoto is 0.23984823888183604 across exactly 15,352 Child pairs versus 0.23743766760756815 across 15,564 Parent pairs, pooled with pair weighting; molecules below six heavy atoms are excluded and the inherited descriptor definition is unchanged. Every batch and task/seed stratum is retained in the audits. These are descriptive diagnostics, not novelty or diversity rewards. All task digests have charged_rate=0.0 and stereocentre_rate=0.0. RDKit detects unassigned tetrahedral centers in 2,685 Child proposals versus 2,820 Parent, with no assigned tetrahedral centers or formally charged atoms on either side. Neutral amines are nevertheless present: the same aliphatic-amine connectivity proxy occurs in 1,077 versus 1,080 proposals, and is not a pKa estimate. Overlapping connectivity flags occur in Child/Parent counts of 239/220 for O-O, 157/168 for nonaromatic O-halogen, 142/155 for nonaromatic N-halogen and 126/122 for acyl halides. These are explicit substructure counts, not stability, toxicity or synthetic-accessibility scores. Familiar moderate-size motifs coexist with tiny remnants, reactive linkages, demanding ring connections and very large combinations of starting motifs. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable at the population level, with individual plausible-looking examples. No synthesis routes, chemical stability measurements, pKa calculations, binding poses or new oracle evaluations are claimed. The formal Anchor is not pooled into the requested code-Parent chemistry baseline. Chemical associations here do not determine mechanism activation, component contribution or a preferred algorithm. Primary authority: policy/requests/r0052-00-improve-L01-molecular-assess-d2c9d622f86d6587.json, especially context.molecular_digest, context.comparison, context.citation_trajectory_paths and focus.artifacts. Request-owned Child trajectories and logs were copied byte-for-byte into owned run-local scratch; each audit records the original path, SHA256, frozen request hash, task, Search seed and run-relative primary inputs. The copies preserve evidence without extending the trusted SMILES citation list. Derived all-cell summary: policy/scratch/r0052-00-molecular/summary.json. Per-task audits and their individual primary trajectory/log files are cited in each task entry.

per_task.generated_character: Across 870 optimizer proposals, heavy atoms span 1 to 119 with median 25; 717 proposals contain rings and 543 contain aromatic atoms. Below-six/above-fifty counts are 110/107 versus Parent 80/99, with Parent median 24. The upper end includes a 22-heavy-atom aza-fused bicyclic aromatic system linked through an ether to an aryl ketimine; a 24-heavy-atom acetamide-bearing, thiocarbonyl-containing constrained nitrogen polycycle; and a 24-heavy-atom phenolic fused nitrogen-ring system with a thiocarbamate. These high examples respectively have three, five and four perceived rings, with three, one and two aromatic rings. Other proposals combine pyrazoline/thioamide, indole/carboxamide, polyaryl ester and acetal motifs. Familiar aromatic ethers and heterocycles make some structures approachable synthetic targets, while the fused connections and stereogenic saturated positions demand route-level scrutiny. The Parent also produces compact nitrogen heterocycles: the difference is which arrangements are reached, not a newly available ring vocabulary. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
